results.label: Proposition 2.1
results.title: Directional passage-time limits
results.summary: For each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, the scaled passage time $n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ has a deterministic limit $g(x)$. The proposition also identifies how that limit changes under scaling, coordinate permutations and addition of directions.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.
results.statement: Assume $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$. There is a deterministic function $g:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ such that, for every fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, $n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}\to g(x)$ almost surely. If $g(x)<\infty$, then $\mathbb E|n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}-g(x)|\to0$. For $a\ge0$ and $x,y\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, $g(ax)=a g(x)$ and $g(x+y)\ge g(x)+g(y)$. Permuting the coordinates of $x$ leaves $g(x)$ unchanged. Use $0\cdot(+\infty)=0$.
results.notes: The guide defines $g$ by the almost-sure directional limit. It separately records the problem with the paper's off-lattice supremum formula (2.3) for signed weights. Uniform convergence over many directions is not part of this proposition.

coverage.scope: The released certificate proves the case $d=2$. The paper states the result for every integer $d\ge2$.

results.label: Proposition 2.2
results.title: Finite values of the shape
results.summary: An integrable weight and a finite explicit upper-tail integral ensure that every value of $g$ is a real number.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.
Define $I_+^{(d)}(F)=\int_0^\infty(1-F(t))^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(F)=\int_{-\infty}^0F(t)^{1/d}\,dt$. These are explicit upper- and lower-tail integrals, respectively.
results.statement: If $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(d)}(F)<\infty$, then $g(x)\in\mathbb R$ for every $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$.

coverage.scope: The released certificate proves the case $d=2$. The paper states the result for every integer $d\ge2$.

results.label: Theorem 2.3
results.title: Continuity at boundary points
results.summary: The shape changes continuously with direction, even when one or more coordinates tend to zero.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

results.statement: Assume $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(d)}(F)<\infty$. If $x_n,x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$ and $|x_n-x|_1\to0$, then $g(x_n)\to g(x)$.

coverage.scope: The released certificate proves the case $d=2$. The paper states the result for every integer $d\ge2$.

results.label: Theorem 2.4
results.title: Shape near a coordinate axis
results.summary: Near the horizontal axis, the first correction to the mean weight is $2\sigma\sqrt\alpha$. Its coefficient depends only on the weight variance.
definitions: Here $d=2$. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.
Define $I_+^{(d)}(F)=\int_0^\infty(1-F(t))^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(F)=\int_{-\infty}^0F(t)^{1/d}\,dt$. These are explicit upper- and lower-tail integrals, respectively.
Write $m=\mathbb E\omega_0$ and $\sigma^2=\mathbb E[(\omega_0-m)^2]$, with $\sigma\ge0$. In this result $d=2$; finiteness of both $I_+^{(2)}(F)$ and $I_-^{(2)}(F)$ implies these moments are finite.
Here $\alpha>0$ is the second coordinate in the direction $(1,\alpha)$; $\alpha\downarrow0$ approaches the horizontal axis.
results.statement: Assume $I_+^{(2)}(F)<\infty$ and $I_-^{(2)}(F)<\infty$. Then $\displaystyle\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}\frac{g(1,\alpha)-m-2\sigma\sqrt\alpha}{\sqrt\alpha}=0$.

coverage.scope: The released certificate covers the full stated result, which is already a two-dimensional statement in the paper.

results.label: Corollary 2.5(i)
results.title: A finite continuous first-passage shape
results.summary: The minimum path weight has a finite directional limit, and this first-passage shape is continuous up to the coordinate boundaries.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.

$S_{u,v}$ is the smallest weight of a directed path from $u$ to $v$, with the same terminal-excluded convention as $L_{u,v}$. Its directional shape is $h(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}S_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x$.
Define $I_+^{(d)}(F)=\int_0^\infty(1-F(t))^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(F)=\int_{-\infty}^0F(t)^{1/d}\,dt$. These are explicit upper- and lower-tail integrals, respectively.
results.statement: If $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_-^{(d)}(F)<\infty$, then $h(x)\in\mathbb R$ for every $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, and $h$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$.

coverage.scope: The release proves $d=2$. The linked first-passage certificate states convergence of expected passage times; Proposition 2.1, applied to the negated weights, identifies this function with the almost-sure directional shape.

results.label: Lemma 3.1
results.title: A probability bound for a maximum of sums
results.summary: The maximum of finitely many sums of independent bounded variables is unlikely to differ much from its expectation.
definitions: $I$ is a finite set. The real random variables $(Y_i)_{i\in I}$ are independent and satisfy $|Y_i|\le b$ almost surely, where $b>0$.
$\mathcal C\ne\varnothing$ is a collection of subsets of $I$. Each $C\in\mathcal C$ has at most $R$ elements, where $R\ge1$ is an integer. Define $Z=\max_{C\in\mathcal C}\sum_{i\in C}Y_i$.
results.statement: For every $u>0$, $\displaystyle\mathbb P(|Z-\mathbb EZ|\ge u)\le\exp\!\left(64-\frac{u^2}{64Rb^2}\right)$. If $b=0$ or $R=0$, all the permitted sums are zero almost surely and the probability on the left is zero.

coverage.scope: The released statement covers an arbitrary probability space and the full finite collection in this lemma. It also treats $b=0$ and $R=0$ explicitly.

results.label: Lemma 3.2
results.title: Changing a small coordinate
results.summary: For bounded weights, adding a sufficiently small coordinate changes $g$ by less than a prescribed amount. One choice of the small coordinate works for all bounded points on the coordinate faces.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.
A coordinate face is the set of points $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$ with one specified coordinate $x_j=0$. Here $1\le j\le d$ and $e_j$ is its coordinate vector.
results.statement: Suppose $\mathbb P(|\omega_0|\le b)=1$ for some finite $b$. For every $R>0$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there is $\delta>0$ such that $|g(x+t e_j)-g(x)|<\varepsilon$ whenever $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, $|x|_1\le R$, $x_j=0$, $1\le j\le d$ and $0\le t\le\delta$.

coverage.scope: The released certificate proves the case $d=2$. The paper states the result for every integer $d\ge2$.

results.label: Lemma 3.3
results.title: Continuity for bounded weights
results.summary: If the site weights are bounded, the shape is continuous at every point, including the coordinate boundaries.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.
results.statement: If $\mathbb P(|\omega_0|\le b)=1$ for some finite $b$, then $g:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d\to\mathbb R$ is continuous.

coverage.scope: The released certificate proves the case $d=2$. The paper states the result for every integer $d\ge2$.

results.label: Proposition 3.4
results.title: Weight bounds for connected sets
results.summary: Among connected sets with $n$ vertices containing the origin, the largest total weight grows at most linearly in $n$. A finite upper-tail integral bounds its expected and almost-sure rates.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.
Define $I_+^{(d)}(F)=\int_0^\infty(1-F(t))^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(F)=\int_{-\infty}^0F(t)^{1/d}\,dt$. These are explicit upper- and lower-tail integrals, respectively.

Let $\mathcal A_n$ consist of all sets $A\subset\mathbb Z^d$ with exactly $n$ vertices, containing $0$, and connected by edges between vertices $u,v$ with $|u-v|_1=1$. These sets are called lattice animals. Define $N(n)=\max_{A\in\mathcal A_n}\sum_{z\in A}\omega_z$.
results.statement: There is a finite constant $c=c(d)$, independent of the weight law, such that whenever $I_+^{(d)}(F)<\infty$, $\mathbb E N(n)\le c n I_+^{(d)}(F)$ for every integer $n>1$, and $\displaystyle\limsup_{n\to\infty}N(n)/n\le c I_+^{(d)}(F)$ almost surely.

coverage.scope: The released certificate proves the case $d=2$. The paper states the result for every integer $d\ge2$.

results.label: Lemma 3.5
results.title: Upper and lower passage bounds
results.summary: The upper-tail integral bounds passage-time means and the shape from above. The mean site weight gives the matching elementary lower bound for the shape.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.
Define $I_+^{(d)}(F)=\int_0^\infty(1-F(t))^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(F)=\int_{-\infty}^0F(t)^{1/d}\,dt$. These are explicit upper- and lower-tail integrals, respectively.
Write $m=\mathbb E\omega_0$. The constant $c=c(d)$ depends only on the dimension. In the maximum below, $z$ ranges over nonnegative lattice points.
results.statement: Under $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(d)}(F)<\infty$, one can choose $c<\infty$ such that $\mathbb E L_{0,z}\le c|z|_1 I_+^{(d)}(F)$ for every $z\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d$; $\displaystyle\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\max_{|z|_1\le n}L_{0,z}\le c I_+^{(d)}(F)$ almost surely; and $|x|_1m\le g(x)\le c|x|_1 I_+^{(d)}(F)$ for every $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$.

coverage.scope: The linked upper bounds are proved for $d=2$. The linked export for the shape lower bound additionally assumes $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^p]<\infty$ for some $p>1$, where $\omega_0^-=\max\{-\omega_0,0\}$. The paper's lemma has the weaker first-moment hypothesis.

results.label: Lemma 3.6
results.title: Effect of capping large weights
results.summary: Moving all site weights into $[-b,b]$ changes the shape by an amount controlled by the parts of the weight distribution beyond those cutoffs.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.
Define $I_+^{(d)}(F)=\int_0^\infty(1-F(t))^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(F)=\int_{-\infty}^0F(t)^{1/d}\,dt$. These are explicit upper- and lower-tail integrals, respectively.

For a cutoff $b>0$, set $\omega_z^{(b)}=\max\{-b,\min\{\omega_z,b\}\}$. Thus all weights are moved into $[-b,b]$. $L_{u,v}^{(b)}$ and $g^{(b)}$ are the passage times and directional shape obtained from these modified weights.
The constant $c=c(d)$ is the one in Lemma 3.5. The integral $\int_{-\infty}^{-b}F(t)\,dt$ equals $\mathbb E[(-b-\omega_0)^+]$, where $a^+=\max\{a,0\}$.
results.statement: Assume $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(d)}(F)<\infty$. For every $b>0$ and $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, $\displaystyle g^{(b)}(x)-|x|_1\int_{-\infty}^{-b}F(t)\,dt\le g(x)\le g^{(b)}(x)+c|x|_1\int_b^\infty(1-F(t))^{1/d}\,dt$. Consequently, for every $R>0$, $\displaystyle\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d,\ |x|_1\le R}|g^{(b)}(x)-g(x)|\to0$ as $b\to\infty$.
results.notes: This compares deterministic shape functions as the weight cutoff grows. It is different from convergence of random passage times as the distance grows.

coverage.scope: The released certificate proves the case $d=2$. The paper states the result for every integer $d\ge2$.

results.label: Lemma 4.1
results.title: A bound for Bernoulli weights
results.summary: For weights that are $1$ with probability $p$ and $0$ otherwise, the shape has an explicit upper bound.
definitions: Here $d=2$. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g_F$ is defined by $g_F(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.
For $p\in[0,1]$, $\operatorname{Ber}(p)$ is the law with mass $p$ at $1$ and mass $1-p$ at $0$. The function $g_{\operatorname{Ber}(p)}$ is its directional last-passage shape.
results.statement: For every $\alpha>0$ and $p\in[0,1]$, $\displaystyle g_{\operatorname{Ber}(p)}(1,\alpha)\le (1+\alpha)p+2\sqrt{\alpha(1+\alpha)p(1-p)}$.

coverage.scope: The released certificate covers the full stated result, which is already a two-dimensional statement in the paper.

results.label: Lemma 4.2
results.title: Changing the weight distribution
results.summary: An explicit integral of the difference between two distribution functions controls the change in their shapes, after accounting for the difference in their means.
definitions: Here $d=2$. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

For $i=1,2$, let $F_i$ be a distribution function, $m_i$ its mean, and $g_{F_i}$ its directional shape. Define $D(F_1,F_2)=\int_{\mathbb R}|F_1(t)-F_2(t)|^{1/2}\,dt$.
results.statement: If $I_+^{(2)}(F_i)$ and $I_-^{(2)}(F_i)$ are finite for $i=1,2$, then for every $\alpha>0$, $\displaystyle|g_{F_1}(1,\alpha)-g_{F_2}(1,\alpha)-(1+\alpha)(m_1-m_2)|\le2\sqrt{\alpha(1+\alpha)}\,D(F_1,F_2)$.

results.label: Lemma 4.3
results.title: Bounded weights with the same mean and variance
results.summary: The distribution can be replaced by one supported in a finite interval while preserving its mean and variance and making a specified integral error as small as desired.
definitions: Here $d=2$. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

The weights $(\omega_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^d}$ are independent with common distribution function $F(t)=\mathbb P(\omega_0\le t)$. A directed path takes steps in $\{e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$. Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g_F$ is defined by $g_F(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^2$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.

results.label: Theorem 5.1
results.title: Passage-time level sets at large times
results.summary: After dividing space by time, the random sets of points with passage time at most $t$ approach the deterministic sets defined by $g$ and $h$.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.

Its weight includes its first vertex and excludes its last vertex. $L_{u,v}$ is the largest weight of such a path from $u$ to $v$.

The shape $g$ is defined by $g(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}L_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, when these deterministic limits exist. Here $\lfloor nx\rfloor$ means coordinatewise rounding down; the probability-one event may depend on $x$.

$S_{u,v}$ is the smallest weight of a directed path from $u$ to $v$, with the same terminal-excluded convention as $L_{u,v}$. Its directional shape is $h(x)=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}S_{0,\lfloor nx\rfloor}$ almost surely for each fixed $x$.
Define $I_+^{(d)}(F)=\int_0^\infty(1-F(t))^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(F)=\int_{-\infty}^0F(t)^{1/d}\,dt$. These are explicit upper- and lower-tail integrals, respectively.

For $t\ge0$, define $B(t)=\{x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d:L_{0,\lfloor x\rfloor}\le t\}$ and $C(t)=\{x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d:S_{0,\lfloor x\rfloor}\le t\}$. Define $B=\{x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d:g(x)\le1\}$ and $C=\{x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d:h(x)\le1\}$.
For a set $A\subset\mathbb R^d$ and a real number $a\ge0$, $aA=\{ax:x\in A\}$. Thus $t^{-1}B(t)$ is the set $B(t)$ shrunk by a factor $t$.
results.statement: Assume $I_+^{(d)}(F)<\infty$ and $I_-^{(d)}(F)<\infty$. (i) If $\mathbb E\omega_0>0$, then almost surely, for every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there is $t_0<\infty$ such that $(1-\varepsilon)B\subseteq t^{-1}B(t)\subseteq(1+\varepsilon)B$ for every $t\ge t_0$. (ii) If there is $c>0$ such that $h(x)\ge c|x|_1$ for every $x\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^d$, the same conclusion holds with $C(t),C$ in place of $B(t),B$.
results.notes: The displayed set inclusions are written in the usual range $0<\varepsilon<1$ so that both dilation factors are nonnegative. The first-passage positive lower bound is an additional premise, not a property that follows from the tail assumptions alone.

coverage.scope: The release proves $d=2$. Its statements also allow $\varepsilon\ge1$ by replacing the inner factor $1-\varepsilon$ with $\max\{1-\varepsilon,0\}$.

results.summary: If both tail integrals are finite, a sufficiently large fixed cutoff makes the error in every distant passage time smaller than a prescribed fraction of its path length.
definitions: Let $d\ge2$ be an integer. The order $u\le v$ means $u_j\le v_j$ for every coordinate $j$. Write $|x|_1=\sum_{j=1}^d|x_j|$, and let $e_j$ be the $j$th coordinate vector.
